transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… what brings me in is I just can’t keep my mind on one thing anymore. Like, I’ll be trying to do something in the shop or the office, and one saw starts up, or somebody walks past, or I suddenly think about another job I need to do, and I’m gone. Completely pulled off. And then I look up and somehow the whole day’s gotten away from me.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself needing to be constantly moving, even when you’re trying to focus on a task?

Yeah… I do, especially when I’m stuck at the desk doing estimates, or in one of those long meetings. I can be sitting there telling myself, just stay put and finish this, and inside I feel all wound up, like I need to stand up or walk around or go check something in the shop. It’s not even because of my wrist anymore—that’s healed—it’s just this feeling like I can’t sit still long enough to get through it.
Do you often act on impulse, like making quick decisions without thinking them through, or feel like you can't wait your turn in conversations or activities?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean… I make quick calls at work sometimes, but that’s carpentry, you know, you’re always deciding things on the fly—measurements, materials, what needs fixing first. My dad used to say “measure twice, cut once,” and I still hear that in my head sometimes, especially when I’m looking at a board and thinking about the cost of messing it up.

But as far as cutting people off or not waiting my turn… I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed that as a big thing. My problem feels more like—well, sorry, what exactly do you mean by impulsive?
Outside of work decisions like measurements or materials, do you find yourself acting on impulse—like interrupting others, making sudden plans, or doing things without thinking them through?

I don’t really know… not in the way you’re saying, I don’t think. I mean, I might decide last minute to run to the hardware store, but then half the time that’s because we’re out of screws or the stain didn’t match, and then I see the cedar boards and remember my neighbor’s fence—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

Interrupting people… I don’t think I do that much. Maybe if I’m excited or I think I’ll forget what I was going to say, but I can’t say it’s a big problem I’ve noticed. Sudden plans, doing things without thinking… I’m not sure. Nothing’s jumping out at me like, “yes, that’s the issue.”
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Um… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say hopeless, exactly. I mean, everybody gets worn down, right? Especially when work piles up and the weather turns and customers want things done yesterday.

As far as losing interest… I still like the things I like, I think. Carpentry’s funny that way—some days sanding a piece feels calming, other days it’s just dust everywhere and you’re wondering why you didn’t buy prefinished trim. Sorry, I’m getting off track.

I guess I haven’t really thought of it as being “down” so much. I’m not sure how to answer that clearly.
Do you often feel worried, on edge, or find it hard to control your anxiety about things at work or in your daily life?

I don’t know… worried, sure, sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s more than anybody else. Work can get stressful when a client changes their mind after you’ve already cut the trim, or when the weather messes with the lumber. You start thinking, well, now I’ve got to redo the whole plan.

But “hard to control anxiety”… I’m not sure. I don’t really think of myself that way. I guess I’d have to know what you mean by on edge. Like nervous all day, or just annoyed because someone moved your tools again? Because that’ll get me going, but I don’t know if that’s anxiety.
Over the last two weeks, have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I’ve been depressed most of the day nearly every day. I mean, I have bad moods, and some days I’m just tired of everything, especially when the day starts with something stupid like the saw blade being dull and then you can’t find the pencil you just had in your hand—sorry.

But hopeless? I don’t know. That feels like a strong word. I wouldn’t say that’s been happening most days, no.
Have you found yourself feeling less interested in things you used to enjoy, or feeling down or discouraged, even if just for several days in a row?

I guess… I haven’t really noticed that in a clear way. Like, I still enjoy things when I actually get myself to them, if that makes sense. Sometimes I’m discouraged because something’s not going right, but then again that happens on any job—one crooked wall and suddenly the whole afternoon is eaten up trying to make trim look straight.

Several days in a row… I’m not sure. I don’t really keep track like that. I wouldn’t say I’ve been sitting around feeling down, exactly. More like I get frustrated and then I move on, or I try to.
Do you often feel a need to be constantly doing something, like you can't relax even when you want to, or that you're always 'on the go'?

Yeah… I guess that does happen, especially if I’m stuck sitting. Like if I have to sit at the desk doing estimates, or sit through some long meeting, I start feeling wound up inside, like I need to get up and move around.

It’s funny because my wrist is healed now, so it’s not like there’s some reason I can’t just sit there and finish the paperwork. I know I’m supposed to stay put and get it done, but inside I’m kind of… revving, I guess. Then I’ll notice some little thing that needs fixing or I’ll want to go check on something, and next thing I know I’m up.
Do you find that you often lose focus or get distracted during tasks that require you to stay concentrated, like reading, planning, or working on detailed projects?

Yes. That’s actually a big part of why I’m here. I just… I cannot keep my mind on one thing anymore.

If I’m trying to read plans or figure out a cut list or even sit down and do an estimate, one saw starts up outside, or somebody walks past the office, or I remember something from another job, and that’s it—I’m gone. Then I’m checking something else, or I get up to ask someone a question, or I’m thinking about whether we ordered the right hinges for a different place… and meanwhile the thing I was supposed to be doing is just sitting there.

And it’s not even always big distractions. Sometimes it’s just a thought. Like, I’ll be looking at measurements and suddenly I’m thinking about a cabinet door from last week, which reminds me of a customer’s dog—he was this little yappy thing, always underfoot—and then ten minutes later I realize I haven’t actually done the math I was staring at. The whole day gets away from me like that.
Can you recall times when you felt physically restless or unable to stay seated, even when you knew you needed to stay put, like during meetings, meals, or when relaxing at home?

Yeah, mostly at the desk or in meetings. If I’m sitting there trying to do estimates, I get this feeling like I’m all wound up inside, like I need to stand up and go check something or move around.

Long meetings are bad for that too. I know I’m supposed to just stay put and listen, or finish the paperwork, and there’s no real reason I can’t—my wrist is healed now, so it’s not like I have that excuse anymore. But my body just doesn’t want to stay in the chair.

At home… I don’t know, I’m not thinking about that as much. It’s more obvious when I’m supposed to be sitting still for work stuff. Then I’m up before I even really decide to be.
Do you often find yourself making mistakes or overlooking details because you’re not paying close enough attention, especially when working on tasks like measurements or paperwork?

Yeah… yes, that’s been happening a lot. The measurements are the worst. I’ll write something down like 36 when it should’ve been 63, or I’ll put the wrong part number on an estimate, and then everyone’s looking at it like, “How did this happen?”

And it’s usually not that I don’t know what I’m doing. I’ve been doing this work a long time. It’s more like my eyes went over it but my brain didn’t catch it. Like on permit forms too—I’ll miss a whole line, and then it comes back, or worse, we only realize after the lumber’s already ordered. Then somebody has to redo the work, and that’s… yeah, that’s embarrassing.

I mean, numbers can look funny anyway if you’re tired—my old shop teacher used to say measure twice, cut once, and I can still hear him saying it—but lately even when I’m trying to be careful, I miss these little details. Then they turn into big problems.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others when they’re talking, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or group settings?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I probably do sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed that as the main thing.

In conversations, I’ll sometimes jump in if I think of something before I lose it, but… I don’t know if that’s interrupting in the way you mean. My sister says everybody in our family talks over each other anyway—Thanksgiving is like a job site with no foreman, just everybody yelling over the table.

But waiting my turn… I don’t think I’m the worst with that. Meetings can be hard, but more because they drag on and people go around in circles. I don’t know. You might have to ask the guys at work if I cut them off. I don’t really keep track of that.

Can you think of times when you’ve missed small details or made mistakes not because you were tired or distracted, but because your mind just didn’t seem to catch them, even when you were looking right at them?

Yeah, that’s exactly what I mean. I’ll be looking right at the estimate, and somehow I put the wrong measurement down—like 36 instead of 63—or the wrong part number. And I swear I’m not trying to rush it, I’m looking at the paper.

Permit forms too… I’ll miss a whole line, and then it gets kicked back, or we don’t catch it until after the lumber’s already ordered. Then somebody has to redo it, and that’s the part that makes me feel awful, because it’s such a small thing but it turns into everybody else’s problem.

It’s like my eyes saw it, but my mind just didn’t grab onto it.
Looking back, were you noticeably distracted, restless, or had trouble focusing when you were a child, say before age 12?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t remember all of it perfectly, but even in grade school, before I was 12, my teachers were always telling my mother, “She’s bright, but careless.” That was the word they used a lot.

I’d lose homework or forget what the instructions were, even if they’d just said them. And I remember sitting there supposed to be doing seatwork, but I’d be staring out the window instead. There was this big maple tree outside one classroom—funny the things you remember—and I could watch the leaves moving forever, and then suddenly everybody else was done and I’d barely started.

So yeah, it was there pretty early. It wasn’t like I was trying to be difficult. I just… didn’t stay with the task somehow.
